doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Father strolling with violin; gigs at fourteen with brother Bob
summary: His brother drove him to big-band gigs at fourteen, he joined the union and played every night.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. Let me ask you about that because I heard you talking about that and that your dad would play in restaurants and he would stroll, he’d pick up the violin and maybe stroll around. And I wondered, did you and your brother Bob actually witness that? Did you go to these places?

My brother may have, since he’s eight years older than me. I did not. But I did — he would take me to gigs when I was fourteen, playing with the big band. I’d be like playing fourth, I was thrilled to death to be there. I couldn’t drive yet, and he would drive me there and he’d sit at the bar and have a beer and he knew everybody in the band. And he was so proud of me you know. He’d sit there, he wasn’t on the gig. But it was wonderful you know. All that happened when I was young, like I say, fourteen years old you know. I joined the union around that time too. I couldn’t drive, but I would do gigs and I was still of course in school so after the gig, you know, I’d sleep in the back seat with the drums or something like that in the car you know. But I always played, no matter where I
was I would always go and take a cab or if I could walk to the jazz club doing one- nighters, every night I’d play. And that’s how you learn.
